page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin beside it. Running head "NOTÆ." at the top, page number 149 at the top right.

main_text.p: plo [?]بيت مارس Domus Mars (num forsan Martis) dicto, tribus ab Aspahano parasangis, antiquitus collocata fuerant, eductis, illud in ignis sacrarium convertisse, ac perpetuas fere lites apud Orientales inter Ignis & Simulachrorum cultores fuisse ab eode difcimus, adeo ut prout alteri alteris superiores evaserint, templa ipsorum aliàs ignium, aliàs simulachrorum cultui inservire jussa sint. Magorum deliria cum dogmatis Christianis (quod idem est ac si coelo tartara) iniquè miscens infanus ille {*}Manes inde impiissimam haeresin conflavit, teste Sharestanio, [?]اخن دينا بيمن Condidit (inquit) religionem inter eam quam Magi & eam quam Christiani profitentur. Origine magum fuisse perhibet, duo, cum Magis rerum principia statuisse Lucem & Tenebras &c. inde illi titulus [?]مانى التنوى i.e. Manes duorum principiorum assertor; referente Gregorio nostro qui cum primò Christianum, postea ad [?]الثنوية seu duorum principiorum haeresin defecisse, & assumpto sibi Messiae nomine, electisq; duodecim discipulis, blasphemias suas per totum Orientem, Indiam usque & Sinam propagasse, scil. [?]اى للعالم اثنين &c. Mundo duos esse Deos, quorum alter bonus, qui [?]معدن النور Fons lucis, alter malus, qui [?]معدن الظلمة Fons tenebrarum, &c. [?]وكان يفرط في تجميس النار وتعظيم شانها quin & modum excessit in igne celebrando, eumque veneratus est ac divinis laudibus efferri voluit, idque propter lumen ipsi innatum, ut è contra terram vilipendi quòd penitus opaca & tenebrosa esset. atque hac (inquit) doctrina, antiquitus apud Persarum[?] recepta fuit, non a Manio, seu Mane primum orta sed quam tantum

page.notes: Right margin, two notes: "* Sive Manius." (beside the line with "Manes", keyed to the asterisk in the text) and "In vita Aureliani Imper." (beside "titulus ... referente Gregorio"). The marginal notes are set in small italic type, so the second is placed at the point where it stands in the margin. Arabic and Persian-Arabic script is transcribed from a low-resolution scan; the Arabic passages are uncertain and are marked [?] throughout. The Arabic on the first line ("بيت مارس") and the Sharestanio title line are doubtful. The word "Persarum" is printed with a ligature-like form, so it is marked [?]. The text of the page appears to continue from the previous page and ends mid-sentence ("quam tantum"), which continues onto the next page. No catchword or signature is visible. Scan is slightly skewed; some margin text is faint.
